title: Computer Languages
excerpt: A journey through the logic of machines. Explore the evolution of syntax and the paradigms that power our digital world—from low-level assembly to modern abstractions.
text1: Explore the world of computer languages, from low-level systems to markup languages.

computer_languages.name: Arcade
computer_languages.description: Arcade is a portable, lightweight expression language written for use with the ArcGIS system. It is used to perform visualization, labeling, and popup calculations.
computer_languages.how_used: Writing scripts inside ArcGIS Pro or Online to format labels or calculate field values dynamically.
computer_languages.semantics: Secure, portable, specialized for GIS features.
computer_languages.data_types: Text, Number, Date, Feature, Geometry.
computer_languages.creator: Esri

computer_languages.name: Terraform
computer_languages.description: Terraform is an open-source infrastructure as code software tool that provides a consistent CLI workflow to manage hundreds of cloud services.
computer_languages.how_used: Defining and provisioning data center infrastructure using a declarative configuration language (HCL).
computer_languages.data_types: Strings, Numbers, Bools, Lists, Maps, Objects.
computer_languages.creator: HashiCorp

computer_languages.name: Swift
computer_languages.description: Swift is a powerful and intuitive programming language for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, and watchOS. Writing Swift code is interactive and fun, the syntax is concise yet expressive.
computer_languages.how_used: The primary language for building apps in the Apple ecosystem.
computer_languages.syntax: Clean, concise, no semicolons needed, expressive.
computer_languages.semantics: Value types (structs) and reference types (classes), ARC for memory management.
computer_languages.data_types: Int, Double, Float, Bool, String, Array, Set, Dictionary, Tuples, Optionals.
computer_languages.control_structures: if/else, switch, for-in, while, repeat-while, guard.
computer_languages.creator: Chris Lattner (Apple)

computer_languages.name: SQLX
computer_languages.description: SQLX is not a language but a modern SQL toolkit for Go and Rust, providing type-safe, compile-time checked SQL queries and async support.
computer_languages.how_used: Writing known, safe SQL interactions in Rust or Go, avoiding full ORMs.
computer_languages.data_types: Maps native language types to SQL types.
computer_languages.creator: Jmoiron (Go) / LaunchBadge (Rust)

computer_languages.name: TypeScript
computer_languages.description: TypeScript is a free and open-source programming language developed and maintained by Microsoft. It is a strict syntactical superset of JavaScript and adds optional static typing to the language.
computer_languages.how_used: Used in large frontend projects (React/Angular) and backend (Node.js) to add type safety.
computer_languages.semantics: Same as JavaScript, but with compile-time type checking.
computer_languages.data_types: All JS types + interfaces, enums, tuples, generics, any, unknown, never.
computer_languages.creator: Anders Hejlsberg

computer_languages.name: Ansible
computer_languages.description: Ansible is an open-source software provisioning, configuration management, and application-deployment tool enabling infrastructure as code.
computer_languages.how_used: Automating server configuration and deployment tasks via SSH.
computer_languages.data_types: Standard YAML types (Strings, Lists, Dictionaries).
main_libraries: Built-in Modules (apt, yum, service, copy, etc.)
computer_languages.creator: Michael DeHaan

computer_languages.name: Julia
computer_languages.description: Julia is a high-level, high-performance, dynamic programming language. It is well suited for numerical analysis and computational science.
computer_languages.how_used: Performance-critical scientific computing.
computer_languages.syntax: Matlab-like, clean, extensive support for math notation.
computer_languages.semantics: Multiple dispatch, dynamic type system, composable.
computer_languages.data_types: Integers, Floats, Strings, Arrays, Tuples, Dictionaries, Structs.
computer_languages.creator: Jeff Bezanson et al.

computer_languages.name: Kotlin
computer_languages.description: Kotlin is a cross-platform, statically typed, general-purpose programming language with type inference. It is designed to interoperate fully with Java.
computer_languages.how_used: Google's preferred language for Android development. Also used for backend services.
computer_languages.semantics: Interop with Java, null safety, coroutines for concurrency.
computer_languages.data_types: Numbers, Booleans, Characters, Strings, Arrays, Classes.
computer_languages.control_structures: if/else, when (switch on steroids), for, while.
computer_languages.compiled_or_interpreted: Compiled to Bytecode (JVM), JS, or Native
computer_languages.creator: JetBrains

computer_languages.name: Dart
computer_languages.description: Dart is a client-optimized language for fast apps on any platform. It is developed by Google and is used to build mobile, desktop, server, and web applications.
computer_languages.how_used: Primary language for the Flutter framework.
computer_languages.data_types: Numbers, Strings, Booleans, Lists, Sets, Maps, Runes, Symbols.
computer_languages.control_structures: if/else, switch, for, while, do/while, try/catch.
computer_languages.compiled_or_interpreted: Compiled (AOT for mobile, JIT for dev) / Transpiled to JS
computer_languages.creator: Lars Bak, Kasper Lund

computer_languages.name: Rust
computer_languages.description: Rust is a multi-paradigm, general-purpose programming language designed for performance and safety, especially safe concurrency. It enforces memory safety without garbage collection.
computer_languages.how_used: Writing operating systems (Linux kernel components), high-performance tools, and secure applications.
computer_languages.syntax: C-like, but with distinct features like lifetimes and ownership.
computer_languages.data_types: Integers, Floats, Booleans, Characters, Tuples, Arrays, Structs, Enums.
computer_languages.creator: Graydon Hoare

computer_languages.name: Go
computer_languages.description: Go is a statically typed, compiled programming language designed at Google. It is syntactically similar to C, but with memory safety, garbage collection, structural typing, and CSP-style concurrency.
computer_languages.how_used: Building high-performance servers, CLI tools (Docker, Kubernetes).
computer_languages.syntax: C-like but simplified, no parentheses in control flow.
computer_languages.data_types: Integers, Floats, Strings, Booleans, Structs, Slices, Maps, Channels.
computer_languages.creator: Robert Griesemer, Rob Pike, Ken Thompson

computer_languages.name: Scratch
computer_languages.description: Scratch is a block-based visual programming language and website targeted primarily at children.
computer_languages.how_used: Teaching kids how to think logically and program.
computer_languages.data_types: Numbers, Strings, Booleans, Lists.
computer_languages.creator: MIT Media Lab

computer_languages.name: Markdown
computer_languages.description: Markdown is a lightweight markup language for creating formatted text using a plain-text editor.
computer_languages.how_used: Widely used for technical documentation, GitHub READMEs, and blogging.
computer_languages.data_types: Text, Lists, Images, Links, Tables.
computer_languages.creator: John Gruber

computer_languages.name: Scala
computer_languages.description: Scala is a strong statically typed general-purpose programming language which supports both object-oriented programming and functional programming.
computer_languages.how_used: Building scalable backend systems and big data processing pipelines (Apache Spark).
computer_languages.semantics: Integrates OOP and Functional programming, runs on JVM.
computer_languages.data_types: All Java types + functional types, Option, Future, Tuple.
computer_languages.creator: Martin Odersky

computer_languages.name: PostGIS
computer_languages.description: PostGIS is a spatial database extender for PostgreSQL object-relational database. It adds support for geographic objects allowing location queries to be run in SQL.
computer_languages.how_used: Storing and querying geospatial data (points, lines, polygons) within a relational database.
computer_languages.data_types: GEOMETRY, GEOGRAPHY, RASTER, TOPOLOGY.
computer_languages.creator: Refractions Research

computer_languages.name: C#
computer_languages.description: C# is a modern, object-oriented, and type-safe programming language. It enables developers to build many types of secure and robust applications that run in the .NET ecosystem.
computer_languages.how_used: Widely used for Windows desktop apps, backend services with ASP.NET Core, and game development with Unity.
computer_languages.syntax: C-style, similar to Java but with more syntactic sugar.
computer_languages.semantics: Pass-by-value (mostly), garbage collected, rich type system.
computer_languages.data_types: Integers, Floats, Decimals, Booleans, Strings, Structs, Classes, Records.
computer_languages.control_structures: if/else, switch, for, foreach, while, do/while, try/catch/finally.
computer_languages.compiled_or_interpreted: Compiled to IL, JIT compiled by CLR
computer_languages.creator: Anders Hejlsberg

computer_languages.name: GDAL
computer_languages.description: The Geospatial Data Abstraction Library (GDAL) is a translator library for raster and vector geospatial data formats.
computer_languages.how_used: Command line tools or via bindings (Python) to read/write GIS formats.
computer_languages.data_types: Datasets, Bands, Features, Geometries.
computer_languages.creator: Frank Warmerdam

computer_languages.name: CSS
computer_languages.description: Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) is a style sheet language used for describing the presentation of a document written in a markup language such as HTML.
computer_languages.how_used: Styles HTML elements (colors, layout, fonts, etc.).
computer_languages.semantics: Defines visual presentation and responsive design.
computer_languages.data_types: Colors, Units, Selectors, Flexbox, Grid.
computer_languages.creator: Håkon Wium Lie

computer_languages.name: JavaScript
computer_languages.description: JavaScript is a programming language that is one of the core technologies of the World Wide Web, alongside HTML and CSS.
computer_languages.how_used: Runs in browsers for interactive UI, and on servers via Node.js.
computer_languages.syntax: C-style syntax, curly braces for blocks.
computer_languages.data_types: Number, String, Boolean, Object, Symbol, Null, Undefined.
computer_languages.control_structures: if/else, switch, for, while, do/while, try/catch.
computer_languages.creator: Brendan Eich

computer_languages.name: Java
computer_languages.description: Java is a high-level, class-based, object-oriented programming language that is designed to have as few implementation dependencies as possible.
computer_languages.how_used: Backend services, large-scale systems, Android mobile apps.
computer_languages.data_types: Primitive types (int, boolean, etc.) and Reference types (Classes).
computer_languages.control_structures: if/else, switch, for, while, do/while, try/catch/finally.
computer_languages.compiled_or_interpreted: Compiled to Bytecode, Interpreted by JVM
computer_languages.creator: James Gosling

computer_languages.name: Ruby
computer_languages.description: Ruby is a dynamic, open source programming language with a focus on simplicity and productivity. It has an elegant syntax that is natural to read and easy to write.
computer_languages.how_used: Mainly used for web development with the Ruby on Rails framework.
computer_languages.syntax: English-like, elegant, very flexible, optional parentheses.
computer_languages.semantics: Everything is an object, dynamic dispatch, blocks/procs/lambdas.
computer_languages.data_types: Numbers, Strings, Symbols, Arrays, Hashes, Ranges.
computer_languages.creator: Yukihiro Matsumoto (Matz)

computer_languages.name: PHP
computer_languages.description: PHP is a popular general-purpose scripting language that is especially suited to web development. It was originally created by Danish-Canadian programmer Rasmus Lerdorf.
computer_languages.how_used: Powers a significant portion of the web (WordPress, etc.). Server-side scripting.
computer_languages.syntax: C-like, embedded in HTML, '$' prefix for variables.
computer_languages.semantics: Request-response lifecycle, loose typing (historically), improving type system.
computer_languages.data_types: String, Integer, Float, Boolean, Array, Object, NULL, Resource.
computer_languages.control_structures: if/else, switch/match, while, do/while, for, foreach.
computer_languages.creator: Rasmus Lerdorf

computer_languages.name: HTML
computer_languages.description: HyperText Markup Language (HTML) is the standard markup language for documents designed to be displayed in a web browser.
computer_languages.how_used: Structures the content of every webpage on the internet.
computer_languages.semantics: Defines the meaning and structure of web content.
computer_languages.data_types: Elements, Attributes, Entities.
computer_languages.creator: Tim Berners-Lee

computer_languages.name: R
computer_languages.description: R is a programming language and free software environment for statistical computing and graphics supported by the R Core Team and the R Foundation for Statistical Computing.
computer_languages.how_used: Data analysis, creating complex statistical models and visualizations.
computer_languages.data_types: Vectors, Lists, Matrices, Arrays, Factors, Data Frames.
computer_languages.creator: Ross Ihaka, Robert Gentleman

computer_languages.name: Lua
computer_languages.description: Lua is a lightweight, high-level, multi-paradigm programming language designed primarily for embedded use in applications.
computer_languages.how_used: Embedded as a scripting engine in larger applications (games like WoW, tools like Redis).
computer_languages.data_types: Nil, Boolean, Number, String, Userdata, Function, Thread, Table.
computer_languages.creator: Roberto Ierusalimschy

computer_languages.name: Python
computer_languages.description: Python is a high-level, general-purpose programming language. Its design philosophy emphasizes code readability with the use of significant indentation.
computer_languages.how_used: Used for backend web development (Django/Flask), data analysis (Pandas), ML (PyTorch/TensorFlow), and scripting.
computer_languages.syntax: Clean, readable, uses indentation for blocks.
computer_languages.semantics: Dynamic, strong typing (mostly). Evaluation is strict.
computer_languages.data_types: Integers, Floats, Strings, Lists, Tuples, Dictionaries, Sets.
computer_languages.creator: Guido van Rossum

computer_languages.name: Haskell
computer_languages.description: Haskell is a general-purpose, statically typed, purely functional programming language with type inference and lazy evaluation.
computer_languages.how_used: Robust systems, teaching functional programming.
computer_languages.data_types: Int, Float, Bool, Lists, Tuples, Custom Types.
computer_languages.creator: Haskell Committee

computer_languages.name: Shell (Bash)
computer_languages.description: Unix shell is a command-line interpreter or shell that provides a command line user interface for Unix-like operating systems. Bash is the most common default shell.
computer_languages.how_used: Automating OS tasks, deployment scripts, file manipulation.
computer_languages.data_types: Strings (mostly), Integers, Arrays.
computer_languages.creator: Brian Fox

computer_languages.name: Perl
computer_languages.description: Perl is a family of high-level, general-purpose, interpreted, dynamic programming languages. 'Perl 5' is the one in common use.
computer_languages.how_used: Text manipulation, One-liners, Legacy systems.
computer_languages.syntax: C-like but flexible, heavy use of sigils ($, @, %).
computer_languages.data_types: Scalars, Arrays, Hashes.
computer_languages.creator: Larry Wall

computer_languages.name: C++
computer_languages.description: C++ is a high-level, general-purpose programming language created by Bjarne Stroustrup as an extension of the C programming language.
computer_languages.how_used: Performance-critical applications, game engines (Unreal), OS kernels.
computer_languages.syntax: C-style, complex, manual memory management options.
computer_languages.data_types: Integers, Floats, Characters, Booleans, Void, User-defined.
computer_languages.creator: Bjarne Stroustrup

computer_languages.name: MATLAB
computer_languages.description: MATLAB is a proprietary multi-paradigm programming language and numeric computing environment developed by MathWorks.
computer_languages.how_used: Solving engineering and mathematical problems, simulations.
computer_languages.data_types: Doubles, Complex Numbers, Characters, Strings, Cells, Structs.
computer_languages.creator: Cleve Moler

computer_languages.name: PROJ
computer_languages.description: PROJ is a generic coordinate transformation software that transforms geospatial coordinates from one coordinate reference system (CRS) to another.
computer_languages.how_used: Underlying engine for GIS software (GDAL, PostGIS, QGIS) to handle map projections.
computer_languages.data_types: Coordinates, CRS definitions.
computer_languages.creator: Gerald Evenden

computer_languages.name: SQL
computer_languages.description: Structured Query Language (SQL) is a domain-specific language used in programming and designed for managing data held in a relational database management system (RDBMS).
computer_languages.how_used: Querying, updating, and managing relational databases.
computer_languages.semantics: Declarative - you specify WHAT you want, not HOW to get it.
computer_languages.data_types: CHAR, VARCHAR, INT, FLOAT, DATE, TIMESTAMP, BLOB, JSON.
computer_languages.control_structures: Generally none (declarative), but extensions like PL/SQL have them.
computer_languages.creator: Donald D. Chamberlin, Raymond F. Boyce

computer_languages.name: C
computer_languages.description: C is a general-purpose, procedural computer programming language supporting structured programming, lexical variable scope, and recursion, with a static type system.
computer_languages.how_used: The foundation of modern computing. Used for writing OS kernels (Linux, Windows) and embedded software.
computer_languages.semantics: Direct memory manipulation, manual memory management.
computer_languages.data_types: char, int, float, double, void, arrays, pointers, structs, unions.
computer_languages.control_structures: if/else, switch, while, do/while, for, goto.
computer_languages.creator: Dennis Ritchie

computer_languages.name: Prolog
computer_languages.description: Prolog is a logic programming language associated with artificial intelligence and computational linguistics.
computer_languages.how_used: Logic puzzles, theorem proving.
computer_languages.data_types: Atoms, Numbers, Variables, Compound Terms.
computer_languages.creator: Alain Colmerauer, Robert Kowalski

computer_languages.name: COBOL
computer_languages.description: COBOL (Common Business-Oriented Language) is a compiled English-like computer programming language designed for business use.
computer_languages.how_used: Mainframe transaction processing.
computer_languages.syntax: Verbose, English-like (ADD X TO Y GIVING Z).
computer_languages.data_types: Pictures (PIC 999), Alphanumeric.
computer_languages.creator: CODASYL (Grace Hopper)

computer_languages.name: Lisp
computer_languages.description: Lisp (List Processing) is a family of programming languages with a long history and a distinctive, fully parenthesized prefix notation.
computer_languages.how_used: Symbolic reasoning, macro systems, editor scripting.
computer_languages.data_types: Atoms, Lists, Symbols.
computer_languages.creator: John McCarthy

computer_languages.name: Fortran
computer_languages.description: Fortran (Formula Translation) is a general-purpose, compiled imperative programming language that is especially suited to numeric computation and scientific computing.
computer_languages.how_used: Legacy scientific codebases, supercomputing.
computer_languages.data_types: Integer, Real, Complex, Logical.
computer_languages.creator: John Backus (IBM)

computer_languages.name: Assembly
computer_languages.description: Assembly language is any low-level programming language in which there is a very strong correspondence between the instruction in the language and the architecture's machine code instructions.
computer_languages.how_used: Writing bootloaders, optimizing critical code paths.
computer_languages.data_types: Bits, Bytes, Words.
computer_languages.creator: Various (Kathleen Booth)
